text: Most of us eat without paying attention. We eat what is served, at the time it is served, and we rarely notice the pattern. But there is pattern. Over a week, your meals repeat, vary, and cluster in ways that tell you something about your household, your region, and your health.

texts.text: Investigate
You will need: your notebook, seven days.
Create a food diary in your notebook, with one entry for each day.
Every evening for one week, write down everything you ate that day — meals, snacks, drinks, everything. Do not leave out the biscuit you ate at 4 p.m.
Write it the same evening. If you wait till Sunday and try to remember Monday, you may forget or misremember items; mark any uncertain entries.
At the end of the week, read the whole table at once.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="119"><tspan x="89">Next,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>compare.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>Ask<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>three<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>classmates<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>show<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>you<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>their<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>tables.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>Find<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.56649"> </tspan>that</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">appears<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>all<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>four<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>diaries,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>appears<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>only<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>one.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>Comparing<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.99187"> </tspan>how</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">we tell what is common from what is particular.</tspan></text>
text: Next, compare. Ask three classmates to show you their tables. Find one food that appears in all four diaries, and one food that appears in only one. Comparing is how we tell what is common from what is particular.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="226"><tspan x="89">Your<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>diaries<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>may<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>share<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>ingredients,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>but<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>check<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>rather<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>than<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>assume<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>this.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>A<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.29904"> </tspan>absent</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">from<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>four<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>diaries<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>may<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>appear<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>another<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>household.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>Four<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>diaries<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>cannot<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.46254"> </tspan>represent</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">the whole class or region.</tspan></text>
text: Your diaries may share ingredients, but check rather than assume this. A food absent from four diaries may appear in another household. Four diaries cannot represent the whole class or region.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="333"><tspan x="89">So<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>even<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>inside<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>single<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>classroom,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>thing.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>It<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>varies.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>The<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>next<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.21440"> </tspan>question</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">is why.</tspan></text>
text: So even inside a single classroom, food is not one thing. It varies. The next question is why.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="465"><tspan x="89">A<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>traveller<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>eating<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>Amritsar,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>Bengaluru<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>Imphal<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>could<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>find<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>different<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>dishes<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.77379"> </tspan>and</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">shared<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>ingredients.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>A<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>regional<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>label<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>does<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>describe<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>every<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>household.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.63203"> </tspan>Compare</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">examples before generalising.</tspan></text>
text: A traveller eating in Amritsar, Bengaluru and Imphal could find different dishes and shared ingredients. A regional label does not describe every household. Compare examples before generalising.

text: That is not an accident, and it is not only a matter of taste. Let us gather the evidence first and explain it afterwards.

texts.text: Investigate
Choose four states of India. Include your own.
For each one, find out: which crops are grown there, which dishes are traditionally eaten, and what people commonly drink.
Use your library, the internet, and — best of all — people. Ask a classmate whose family comes from another state. Ask a neighbour.
Record your findings in your notebook using the headings in Table 3.2. The printed rows are examples.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1148"><tspan x="89">Local<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>crops<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>influence<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>traditions,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>but<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>proximity<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>alone<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>does<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>guarantee<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05444"> </tspan>the</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">cheapest or freshest food. Transport, storage, season and farming costs also matter.</tspan></text>
text: Local crops can influence food traditions, but proximity alone does not guarantee the cheapest or freshest food. Transport, storage, season and farming costs also matter.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="175"><tspan x="89">Soil,<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>rainfall<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>temperature<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>affect<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>which<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>crops<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>grow<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>well.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>Rice<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>often<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>grown<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.76981"> </tspan>in</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">flooded<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>fields,<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>though<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>all<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>rice<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>requires<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>standing<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>water.<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>Ragi<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>tolerate<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.05951"> </tspan>relatively</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">dry conditions. Farmers can also change irrigation and soil management.</tspan></text>
text: Soil, rainfall and temperature affect which crops grow well. Rice is often grown in flooded fields, though not all rice requires standing water. Ragi can tolerate relatively dry conditions. Farmers can also change irrigation and soil management.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="282"><tspan x="89">Soil<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>climate<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>whole<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>story.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>Culture,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>religion<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>history<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>all<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>shape<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.97672"> </tspan>what</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>community<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>eats<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>what<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>it<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>avoids.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>Two<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>families<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>same<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>street,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>growing<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47742"> </tspan>food</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">from the same fields, may cook very differently.</tspan></text>
text: Soil and climate are not the whole story. Culture, religion and history all shape what a community eats and what it avoids. Two families in the same street, growing food from the same fields, may cook very differently.

text: Investigate 1. Choose someone at least fifty years older than you — a grandparent, a neighbour, a retired teacher. 2. Prepare your questions before you meet them. Write them down. What changed, and when did it change? 3. Listen more than you talk. Write their answers in their words, not yours. 4. Bring your notes to class and pool them with your classmates'.

texts.text: Investigate
Choose someone at least fifty years older than you — a grandparent, a neighbour, a retired teacher.

Prepare your questions before you meet them. Write them down. Good starting points: What did you eat as a child that you still eat today? What did you eat then that you never eat now? How was the food cooked, and on what? How long did the cooking take? What changed, and when did it change?
Listen more than you talk. Write their answers in their words, not yours.
Bring your notes to class and pool them with your classmates'.

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1127.1160337552742"><tspan x="89">Partly<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>because<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>technology<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>arrived.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>Gas<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>connections,<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>electricity<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44722"> </tspan>affordable</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">appliances<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>reached<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>ordinary<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>households,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>once<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>tool<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>saves<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>an<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>hour<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>day<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.72219"> </tspan>is</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">available, people use it.</tspan></text>
text: Partly because the technology arrived. Gas connections, electricity and affordable appliances reached ordinary households, and once a tool that saves an hour a day is available, people use it.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="119"><tspan x="89">Partly<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>because<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>transport<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>improved.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>Roads,<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>railways<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>cold<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>storage<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>mean<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.44425"> </tspan>a</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">fruit<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>grown<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>Himachal<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>be<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>sold<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>Chennai.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>Foods<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>were<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>once<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>purely<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.22260"> </tspan>local</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">became available everywhere, and cuisines began to borrow from each other.</tspan></text>
text: Partly because transport improved. Roads, railways and cold storage mean that a fruit grown in Himachal can be sold in Chennai. Foods that were once purely local became available everywhere, and cuisines began to borrow from each other.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="226"><tspan x="89">Television,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>phones<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>internet<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>spread<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>recipes<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>beyond<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>region.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>To<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>test<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61891"> </tspan>a</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">claim<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>about<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>how<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>quickly<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>dish<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>spread,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>we<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>would<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>need<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>dated<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>evidence<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>from<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.24278"> </tspan>several</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">places.</tspan></text>
text: Television, phones and the internet can spread recipes beyond a region. To test a claim about how quickly one dish spread, we would need dated evidence from several places.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="333"><tspan x="89">Change<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>this<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>kind<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>brings<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>real<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>gains.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>Cooking<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>takes<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>less<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>time<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>which<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>matters<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.27817"> </tspan>most</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">to<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>women<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>who<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>have<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>historically<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>done<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>most<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>it.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>Fuel-efficient<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>stoves<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>mean<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.98541"> </tspan>less</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">smoke indoors, and less smoke means healthier lungs.</tspan></text>
text: Change of this kind brings real gains. Cooking takes less time — which matters most to the women who have historically done most of it. Fuel-efficient stoves mean less smoke indoors, and less smoke means healthier lungs.

text: Changes can also reduce the use of familiar grains or cooking skills. Whether a replacement is more nourishing depends on its ingredients, preparation and quantity. Compare examples rather than assuming that older or newer food is better.

text: Smoke in the kitchen A wood or dung chulha burning indoors fills a kitchen with fine smoke. Breathing that smoke for years damages the lungs and the heart, and the person standing closest to the stove breathes the most of it. This is one reason governments have worked to bring clean cooking fuel to rural households: a better stove is a health measure, not just a convenience.

text: Different foods carry different components in different amounts. That is why no single food keeps a person well, and why the mixture on the plate matters as much as the items on it.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="276"><tspan x="89">Glucose<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>simple<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>sugar<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>carbohydrate.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>Cells<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>release<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>energy<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>from<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.05795"> </tspan>glucose.</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">Starch<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>also<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>carbohydrate;<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>digestion<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>breaks<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>it<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>down<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>into<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>smaller<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>sugars<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74841"> </tspan>before</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">absorption. Foods supply mixtures, so a banana is not a dose of pure glucose.</tspan></text>
text: Glucose is a simple sugar and a carbohydrate. Cells can release energy from glucose. Starch is also a carbohydrate; digestion breaks it down into smaller sugars before absorption. Foods supply mixtures, so a banana is not a dose of pure glucose.

Ordinary table sugar is a carbohydrate too.</tspan></text>
text: We rarely eat pure glucose. We eat carbohydrates in the form of cereals — wheat, rice, maize, jowar; in root vegetables — potato and sweet potato; and in fruits — banana, mango, pineapple, sugarcane. Ordinary table sugar is a carbohydrate too.

The body can use fat for energy or store it; it does not automatically store all dietary fat. Stored fat also cushions organs and reduces heat loss. These functions do not establish a special need for laddoos in winter.

text: Fats come from plants and from animals. Plant sources include groundnut, walnut, cashew, almond, pistachio, coconut, sesame seed, pumpkin seed, sunflower seed, soya bean and the oils pressed from them. Animal sources include butter, ghee, curd and milk.

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="175"><tspan x="89">Carbohydrates<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>fats<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>supply<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>energy,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>fats<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>also<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>form<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>parts<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>cells.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>Proteins<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.55931"> </tspan>have</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">an<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>essential<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>role<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>building<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>repairing<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>tissues.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>These<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>job<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>labels<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>overlap;<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>they<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.38127"> </tspan>are</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">not exclusive compartments.</tspan></text>
text: Carbohydrates and fats supply energy, and fats also form parts of cells. Proteins have an essential role in building and repairing tissues. These job labels overlap; they are not exclusive compartments.

text: Consider what a body has to do besides move. A six-year-old grows into a sixteen-year-old. A cut on your hand closes over in a week. Hair grows, nails grow, muscle thickens with training. All of that is construction work, and construction needs material.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="420"><tspan x="89">The material is protein.</tspan></text>

text: Proteins are used to build new tissue and repair damaged tissue. This is why the diet of a growing child must contain enough protein, and why an athlete training for strength needs more than a person who is not. A body short of protein cannot grow properly, however much energy it is given — you cannot build a wall out of firewood.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="659"><tspan x="89">Pulses,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>soya<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>beans,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>nuts<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>seeds<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>supply<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>protein.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>Milk,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>curd,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>paneer,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>eggs,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>fish<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.61170"> </tspan>and</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">meat<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>other<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>sources.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>Compare<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>amounts<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>as<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>well<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>as<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>presence:<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>fresh<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.81167"> </tspan>mushrooms</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">contain protein but are mostly water and supply less per usual serving than pulses.</tspan></text>
text: Pulses, soya beans, nuts and seeds supply protein. Milk, curd, paneer, eggs, fish and meat are other sources. Compare amounts as well as presence: fresh mushrooms contain protein but are mostly water and supply less per usual serving than pulses.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="766"><tspan x="89">Because<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>job<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>they<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>do,<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>protein-rich<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>foods<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>called<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>body-building<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>foods<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="-0.02239"> </tspan>while</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">carbohydrates and fats, which supply energy, are together called energy-giving foods.</tspan></text>
text: Because of the job they do, protein-rich foods are called body-building foods — while carbohydrates and fats, which supply energy, are together called energy-giving foods.

<text class="se-copy" x="89" y="281"><tspan x="89">Mushrooms belong to the fungi, not the plants.</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">They obtain nutrients from organic matter rather</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">than making sugars by photosynthesis. Fresh edible</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">mushrooms contain water, fibre and nutrients, but</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">are not interchangeable with pulses as a protein</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">source. Never taste a wild mushroom to identify it.</tspan></text>
text: Mushrooms belong to the fungi, not the plants. They obtain nutrients from organic matter rather than making sugars by photosynthesis. Fresh edible mushrooms contain water, fibre and nutrients, but are not interchangeable with pulses as a protein source. Never taste a wild mushroom to identify it.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="600"><tspan x="89">Carbohydrates,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>fats<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>proteins<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>components<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>we<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>eat<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>by<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>spoonful.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>There<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.05095"> </tspan>is</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">another<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>set<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>we<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>need<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>amounts<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>so<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>small<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>they<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>measured<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>milligrams<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.23244"> </tspan>and</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">yet a person who goes without them falls seriously ill.</tspan></text>
text: Carbohydrates, fats and proteins are the components we eat by the spoonful. There is another set that we need in amounts so small they are measured in milligrams — and yet a person who goes without them falls seriously ill.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="707"><tspan x="89">The<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>strongest<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>way<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>see<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>what<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>these<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>components<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>do<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>look<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>at<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>what<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>happens<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.51273"> </tspan>when</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">they<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>missing.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>Read<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>two<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>cases<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>below<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>work<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>out<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>answer<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>yourself<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.30464"> </tspan>before</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">reading on.</tspan></text>
text: The strongest way to see what these components do is to look at what happens when they are missing. Read the two cases below and work out the answer yourself before reading on.

html: <text class="se-heading" x="89" y="819.06"><tspan x="89">Case 1 — The sailors' disease</tspan></text>

<image class="science-illustration" href="../../figures/reference/food/p011-sailing-ship.png" x="657" y="847" width="306" height="235" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"><title>sailing ship</title></image>

<text class="se-copy" x="89" y="870"><tspan x="89">On long sea voyages in earlier centuries, sailors fell</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">ill in a particular way. Their gums swelled and bled,</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">their teeth loosened, old wounds reopened, and</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">many died — often months from any battle or storm.</tspan></text>
text: On long sea voyages in earlier centuries, sailors fell ill in a particular way. Their gums swelled and bled, their teeth loosened, old wounds reopened, and many died — often months from any battle or storm.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1133"><tspan x="89">In<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>May<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>1747,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>James<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>Lind<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>compared<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>six<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>treatments<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>among<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>twelve<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>sailors<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>with<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.04351"> </tspan>scurvy,</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">two<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>sailors<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>per<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>treatment.<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>The<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>pair<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>receiving<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>oranges<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>lemons<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>improved<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.25340"> </tspan>most</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">rapidly.</tspan></text>
text: In May 1747, James Lind compared six treatments among twelve sailors with scurvy, two sailors per treatment. The pair receiving oranges and lemons improved most rapidly.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1240"><tspan x="89">The condition is called scurvy.</tspan></text>

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1285"><tspan x="89">Now<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>interpret<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>Case<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>1.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>Lind's<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>sailors<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>were<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>short<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>ships<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>carried<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.96758"> </tspan>salted</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">meat<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>dry<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>biscuit<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>quantity.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>They<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>were<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>short<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>something<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>present<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.08024"> </tspan>lemons</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">and oranges and absent from salted meat.</tspan></text>
text: Now interpret Case 1. Lind's sailors were not short of food — ships carried salted meat and dry biscuit in quantity. They were short of something present in lemons and oranges and absent from salted meat.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="119"><tspan x="89">That<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>something<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>now<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>called<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>C.<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>Scurvy<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>caused<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>by<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>lack<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>C<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.18333"> </tspan>in</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">the<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>diet,<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>it<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>prevented<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>cured<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>by<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>foods<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>contain<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>it<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>citrus<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>fruits<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.68454"> </tspan>like</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">lemon and orange, and also amla, guava and green chilli.</tspan></text>
text: That something is now called Vitamin C. Scurvy is caused by a lack of Vitamin C in the diet, and it is prevented and cured by foods that contain it — citrus fruits like lemon and orange, and also amla, guava and green chilli.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="282"><tspan x="89">The<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>comparison<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>supplied<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>evidence<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>favouring<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>citrus<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>fruit<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>over<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>other<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.00007"> </tspan>treatments</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">tested.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>It<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>did<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>identify<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>C,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>two<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>sailors<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>per<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>treatment<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>small<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.45792"> </tspan>sample.</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">More observations and later research were needed to establish the cause.</tspan></text>
text: The comparison supplied evidence favouring citrus fruit over the other treatments tested. It did not identify Vitamin C, and two sailors per treatment is a small sample. More observations and later research were needed to establish the cause.

text: Lind's sailors ate plenty of food and still fell ill. What does that tell you about the difference between eating enough and eating well?

text: Case 2 — The swelling in the neck

html: <image class="science-illustration" href="../../figures/reference/food/p012-himalayan-village.png" x="657" y="584" width="306" height="235" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"><title>himalayan village</title></image>

<text class="se-copy" x="89" y="607"><tspan x="89">In the 1960s, Indian scientists studying the</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">Himalayan region and the northern plains found</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">that a large number of people there had a visible</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">swelling at the front of the neck. It was common in</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">some districts and rare in others only a few hundred</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">kilometres away.</tspan></text>
text: In the 1960s, Indian scientists studying the Himalayan region and the northern plains found that a large number of people there had a visible swelling at the front of the neck. It was common in some districts and rare in others only a few hundred kilometres away.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="870"><tspan x="89">Following<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>scientists'<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>findings,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>Government<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>India<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>promoted<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>addition<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.32006"> </tspan>of</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">iodine<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>common<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>salt<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>iodised<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>salt.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>Where<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>people<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>switched<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>it,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.74028"> </tspan>swellings</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">became far less common.</tspan></text>
text: Following the scientists' findings, the Government of India promoted the addition of iodine to common salt — iodised salt. Where people switched to it, the swellings became far less common.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="977"><tspan x="89">The condition is called goitre.</tspan></text>

texts.text: How It Works

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1078"><tspan x="89">Iodine<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>deficiency<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>enlarge<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>thyroid<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>gland,<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>causing<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>goitre.<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>Diets<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>relying<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.20471"> </tspan>on</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">crops<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>from<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>iodine-poor<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>soil<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>contribute.<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>But<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>neck<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>swelling<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>have<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.85132"> </tspan>other</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">causes: symptoms alone do not diagnose a nutrient deficiency.</tspan></text>
text: Iodine deficiency can enlarge the thyroid gland, causing goitre. Diets relying on crops from iodine-poor soil can contribute. But a neck swelling can have other causes: symptoms alone do not diagnose a nutrient deficiency.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="119"><tspan x="89">Iodised<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>salt<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>way<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>supply<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>small,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>controlled<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>amount<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>iodine<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>through<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.93855"> </tspan>widely</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">used<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>ingredient.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>This<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>does<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>mean<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>eating<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>extra<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>salt;<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>it<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>means<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>using<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>iodised<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.61568"> </tspan>salt</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">within the usual limited amount.</tspan></text>
text: Iodised salt is a way to supply a small, controlled amount of iodine through a widely used ingredient. This does not mean eating extra salt; it means using iodised salt within the usual limited amount.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="226"><tspan x="89">You<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>have<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>probably<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>read<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>words<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>"iodised<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>salt"<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>on<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>packet<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>without<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>thinking<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.29848"> </tspan>about</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">them.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>They<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>mean<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>common<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>salt<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>which<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>small<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>measured<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>quantity<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>iodine<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.03217"> </tspan>salts</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">has been added.</tspan></text>
text: You have probably read the words "iodised salt" on a packet without thinking about them. They mean common salt to which a small measured quantity of iodine salts has been added.

html: <text class="se-heading" x="89" y="338.06"><tspan x="89">Vitamin C and iodine are examples of a larger group: the</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="38">vitamins and minerals.</tspan></text>
text: Vitamin C and iodine are examples of a larger group: the vitamins and minerals.

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="802"><tspan x="89">In<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>Little<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>Rann<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>Kutch,<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>Agariya<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>salt<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>workers<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>pump<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>underground<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>brine<tspan data-gap="" dx="5.14625"> </tspan>into</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">evaporation<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>pans.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>Water<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>evaporates<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>salt<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>crystallises.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>This<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>example<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>connects<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.93371"> </tspan>a</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">food ingredient to separation by evaporation and to the people who produce it.</tspan></text>
text: In the Little Rann of Kutch, Agariya salt workers pump underground brine into evaporation pans. Water evaporates and salt crystallises. This example connects a food ingredient to separation by evaporation and to the people who produce it.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="909"><tspan x="89">Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>C<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>iodine<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>two<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>many.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>Each<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>each<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>mineral<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>has<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>its<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.18562"> </tspan>own</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">job,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>its<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>own<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>sources,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>its<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>own<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>set<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>symptoms<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>when<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>body<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>runs<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.09840"> </tspan>short.</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">Together they are what keep the body's defences and daily processes working.</tspan></text>
text: Vitamin C and iodine are two of many. Each vitamin and each mineral has its own job, its own food sources, and its own set of symptoms when the body runs short. Together they are what keep the body's defences and daily processes working.

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="824.5052410901468"><tspan x="89">A<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan><tspan class="se-bold">nutrient</tspan><tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>substance<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>body<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>needs<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>for<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>energy,<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>growth,<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>repair<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>or<tspan data-gap="" dx="6.26836"> </tspan>normal</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">functioning.<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>Carbohydrates,<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>fats,<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>proteins,<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>vitamins<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>minerals<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="9.81336"> </tspan>nutrient</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">groups; water is an essential nutrient too.</tspan></text>
text: A **nutrient** is a substance the body needs for energy, growth, repair or normal functioning. Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and minerals are nutrient groups; water is an essential nutrient too.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="931.5052410901468"><tspan x="89">The<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>labels<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>energy-giving,<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>body-building<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>protective<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>highlight<tspan data-gap="" dx="14.43288"> </tspan>important</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">functions,<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>but<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>jobs<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>overlap.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>Proteins<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>supply<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>energy,<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>fats<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>form<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>parts<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.28057"> </tspan>cells,</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">and vitamins and minerals support many processes.</tspan></text>
text: The labels energy-giving, body-building and protective highlight important functions, but the jobs overlap. Proteins can supply energy, fats form parts of cells, and vitamins and minerals support many processes.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1038.5052410901467"><tspan x="89">Vitamins<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>minerals<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>help<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>body<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>processes<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>work<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>normally.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>Calling<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>them<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.09938"> </tspan>protective</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">does not mean that eating one food prevents every disease or treats every symptom.</tspan></text>
text: Vitamins and minerals help body processes work normally. Calling them protective does not mean that eating one food prevents every disease or treats every symptom.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="1114.5052410901467"><tspan x="89">This<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>why<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>you<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>told<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>drink<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>milk,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>eat<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>green<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>vegetables,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>eat<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>fruit,<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>eat<tspan data-gap="" dx="1.47354"> </tspan>whole</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">grains<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>rather<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>than<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>only<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>polished<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>ones<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>because<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>these<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>foods<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>filling,<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.84220"> </tspan>but</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">because they carry the nutrients that nothing else will supply.</tspan></text>
text: This is why you are told to drink milk, eat green vegetables, eat fruit, and eat whole grains rather than only polished ones — not because these foods are filling, but because they carry the nutrients that nothing else will supply.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="826" x="113" y="190"><tspan x="113">Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>D<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>on<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>list,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>but<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>of<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>its<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>sources<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>food<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>at<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>all.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>Which<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.82542"> </tspan>—</tspan><tspan x="113" dy="31">and what does that tell you about spending time outdoors?</tspan></text>

html: <text class="se-heading" x="89" y="286.06"><tspan x="89">3.4 Cooking, Roughage and Water</tspan></text>

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="337"><tspan x="89">Have<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>you<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>noticed<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>raw<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>carrot<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>snaps<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>boiled<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>one<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>bends?<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>That<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>spinach<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.61083"> </tspan>loses</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">its bright green in the pan?</tspan></text>
text: Have you noticed that a raw carrot snaps and a boiled one bends? That spinach loses its bright green in the pan?

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="413"><tspan x="89">Heat<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>changes<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>food,<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>only<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>ways<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>we<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>can<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>see.<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>Some<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>nutrients<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>Vitamin<tspan data-gap="" dx="2.54731"> </tspan>C</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">among<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>them<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>partly<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>destroyed<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>by<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>high<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>heat.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>Washing<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>vegetables<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>fruit<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.83034"> </tspan>after</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">cutting or peeling them washes some vitamins away as well.</tspan></text>
text: Heat changes food, and not only in ways we can see. Some nutrients — Vitamin C among them — are partly destroyed by high heat. Washing vegetables and fruit after cutting or peeling them washes some vitamins away as well.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="520"><tspan x="89">Two<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>sensible<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>conclusions<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>follow.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>First,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>include<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>some<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>fruit<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>raw<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>vegetables<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.48899"> </tspan>your</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">diet<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>so<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>that<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>not<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>everything<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>you<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>eat<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>has<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>been<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>through<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>hot<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>pan.<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>Second,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>wash<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.04678"> </tspan>produce</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">before you cut it, not after.</tspan></text>
text: Two sensible conclusions follow. First, include some fruit and raw vegetables in your diet so that not everything you eat has been through a hot pan. Second, wash produce before you cut it, not after.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="627"><tspan x="89">But<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>do<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>wash<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>it.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>Thoroughly,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>every<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>time.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>The<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>vitamins<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>lost<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>to<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>washing<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.91435"> </tspan>small</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">price against the dirt, pesticide residue and germs that washing removes.</tspan></text>
text: But do wash it. Thoroughly, every time. The vitamins lost to washing are a small price against the dirt, pesticide residue and germs that washing removes.

text: Dietary fibre, or roughage, comes mainly from plant foods such as whole grains, pulses, fruit and vegetables. Our own digestive enzymes do not break it down, although gut microbes can break down some fibre. Fibre helps bowel function; constipation can have several causes.

text: Water dissolves and transports substances, helps remove waste in urine and helps regulate temperature through sweating and evaporation. Needs vary with activity and weather. Water is a nutrient, not a source of food energy.

text: Coluthur Gopalan set out to find out. Over his career he and his colleagues analysed the nutritional content of more than five hundred Indian foods — not foods from foreign tables, but the grains, pulses, vegetables and greens that Indian households actually cooked. It is difficult, unglamorous laboratory work, and it produced something India had never had: reliable numbers for its own diet.

text: He then led large surveys of what Indians were eating and how healthy they were. The surveys found widespread shortages of protein and energy, particularly among children — not in a few unlucky families, but across whole populations.

text: The national school nutrition programme began in 1995 and developed into the cooked school-meal programme now called PM POSHAN. Nutrition research helped shape school feeding policy. A programme date alone does not prove its effects: those require measurements of children and meals.

texts.text: Investigate
You will need: the same food samples; plain paper.
Use cooking oil as a positive control and water as a negative control. Keep sample amounts and waiting times alike. Record observations before interpreting them.
Take a small piece of each food from the iodine investigation.
Place each on a separate piece of paper. Label the papers.
Fold the paper over the food and press firmly. Do not tear it.
If a food is watery, set the paper aside until it dries — a wet patch is not an oily patch, and confusing the two will ruin your result.
Hold each paper up to the light.

Teacher demonstration — precautions. • Copper sulfate and caustic soda are harmful chemicals. Do not touch them unless your teacher tells you to. Your teacher will demonstrate this activity. Read the precautions before anything else.
The teacher should include egg white as a positive control and water as a negative control. Keep sample amounts and waiting times alike. Record observations before interpreting them.
You will need: the same food samples; pestle and mortar; clean test tubes; two droppers; copper sulfate solution; caustic soda solution.
Grind each food sample into a paste or powder with the pestle and mortar.
Put about half a teaspoon of each into a separate clean test tube.
Add two or three teaspoons of water to each tube and shake well.
Using one dropper, add two drops of copper sulfate solution to each tube.
Using a different dropper, add ten drops of caustic soda solution to each tube.
Shake, then leave the tubes undisturbed for a few minutes.

text: Does everyone need the same food in the same amounts? Clearly not. A twelve-year-old is still growing and needs more protein for her size than her grandfather does. A farmhand doing heavy work all day needs more energy than someone at a desk. A person recovering from illness has different needs again. Requirements shift with age, sex, level of physical activity, state of health and way of life. A balanced diet is one that supplies all the nutrients a particular person needs, in the right amounts, together with enough roughage and water. Note the phrase a particular person. There is no single balanced diet for everybody — the idea only means anything once you say who is eating.

Then, within a few decades, they largely disappeared from urban plates, pushed aside by polished rice and refined wheat.

text: Millets are small-grained cereals, so they supply carbohydrate like any cereal. What sets them apart is what comes with the carbohydrate: substantially more dietary fibre than polished rice, along with iron, calcium and B vitamins. Because of this they are often called nutri-cereals — cereals that carry protective nutrients alongside energy.

text: Many millets tolerate relatively dry conditions and can need less irrigation than flooded rice. Water use still depends on crop, yield, climate and farming practice. Compare like growing conditions before making a numerical claim.

text: Millets can add variety and nutrients and can suit dry regions. This does not make every millet superior to every rice dish on every measure.

html: <text class="se-heading" x="89" y="200.06"><tspan x="89">Would millets alone be enough?</tspan></text>

<text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="251"><tspan x="89">No<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>—<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>reason<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>worth<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>understanding.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>Millets<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>are<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>strong<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>on<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.48642"> </tspan>carbohydrate,</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">fibre<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>several<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>minerals,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>but<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>weak<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>on<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>some<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>nutrients<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>body<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>needs,<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>no<tspan data-gap="" dx="0.41212"> </tspan>cereal</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">supplies<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>everything.<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>Eaten<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>with<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>dal,<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>vegetables,<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>milk<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>or<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>curd,<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>millets<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>make<tspan data-gap="" dx="7.64799"> </tspan>an</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">excellent meal. Eaten alone, they leave gaps.</tspan></text>
text: No — and the reason is worth understanding. Millets are strong on carbohydrate, fibre and several minerals, but weak on some nutrients the body needs, and no cereal supplies everything. Eaten with dal, vegetables, milk or curd, millets make an excellent meal. Eaten alone, they leave gaps.

text: Aarav's lunch had rice in it. Ira's had wheat. Neither grew in the school. Follow a chapati backwards from the plate and you find a chain of work. A farmer prepares soil, sows wheat, waters and tends it for months, and harvests it. The grain is threshed and winnowed to separate it from the chaff. It is stored, often for months. It is transported to a mill and ground into flour. The flour is packed, transported again, and sold in a shop. Someone buys it, carries it home, kneads it, and cooks the chapati.

text: Food miles is the distance food travels from producer to consumer. A shorter journey may reduce transport, but total cost, freshness and emissions also depend on farming, storage, transport method and waste. Distance alone cannot establish the best choice.

text: People across India eat widely different food, and the difference is not random. It follows the crops that grow in each region, which follow soil and climate, and is then shaped by culture, religion and taste.

The changes brought real gains and some real losses.</tspan></text>
text: Culinary practices have changed sharply within living memory — from chulha to gas stove, from sil-batta to mixer-grinder — driven by new technology, better transport and faster communication. The changes brought real gains and some real losses.

text: • Carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and minerals are nutrient groups studied here. Water is also an essential nutrient. Food supplies dietary fibre as well.

text: • Carbohydrates and fats supply energy and are called energy-giving foods. Fat carries more energy per gram than carbohydrate and is the body's store.

text: • Proteins build and repair the body and are called body-building foods. Growing children and athletes need proportionally more.

html: <text class="se-copy" data-measure="874" x="89" y="938"><tspan x="89">A<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>balanced<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>diet<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>supplies<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>all<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>nutrients<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>a<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>particular<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>person<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>needs,<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>in<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>the<tspan data-gap="" dx="4.64517"> </tspan>right</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">amounts,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>with<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>enough<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>roughage<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>and<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>water.<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>What<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>is<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>balanced<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>depends<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>on<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>age,<tspan data-gap="" dx="3.11771"> </tspan>sex,</tspan><tspan x="89" dy="31">activity, health and way of life.</tspan></text>
text: A balanced diet supplies all the nutrients a particular person needs, in the right amounts, with enough roughage and water. What is balanced depends on age, sex, activity, health and way of life.
